title: Stop Poisoning the Southall Community! (CrowdJustice case page, incl. Updates 1-2)
summary: CASH's crowdfunding page to instruct environmental lawyers (Clyde & Co listed) for a public-nuisance claim against Berkeley Group, possibly also Ealing Council and the Environment Agency. Funded 31 July 2019; GBP 6,222 from 94 pledges against a GBP 10,000 stretch target (case text says minimum GBP 25,000). Two updates (24 Sep 2019: joint CASH/Extinction Rebellion die-in at Ealing Town Hall on 14 Sep 2019; 15 Oct 2019: Daily Mirror coverage).
notes: Date = 'Funded on' date; page creation date not shown. No update after Oct 2019 announcing that legal action actually began. Lists CASH social accounts: facebook.com/CleanAirSouthall, twitter.com/cashcampaigners, instagram.com/cleanairforsouthallandhayes, YouTube channel UChFHFUx8LL0v7u5NIwyImZQ.

title: Clean Air for Southall and Hayes! Stop the contaminated old gasworks polluting our kids! (Change.org petition)
summary: Founding petition of the campaign, started by resident David Marsden, demanding Berkeley Group install effective odour controls and halt the on-site 'soil hospital'; names Ealing Council, the EA, MP Virendra Sharma and Berkeley staff as unresponsive. Closed with 918 supporters.
notes: cash_authored=true on the basis that Marsden described himself (EALING.NEWS, 29 Oct 2022) as co-founder of the group with Angela Fonso; the petition is in his name, not CASH's. Decision-maker list was edited later (names Peter Mason as Leader, i.e. after May 2021). Wayback not checked.

title: Change.org petition updates, 30 Jul 2018 (letter to Simon Dawkins, EA) and 12 Aug 2018 (public meeting at Roxy's)
summary: Two petition updates by David Marsden: an open letter asking the Environment Agency officer visiting the site to force a halt to soil-hospital operations during the 2018 heatwave, and a report of door-knocking on Beaconsfield Road plus notice of a public meeting on 13 Aug 2018.
notes: Second update URL: .../u/23131227. An earlier update (u/23026548) was not retrieved.

title: Open letter from CASH to Cllr Peter Mason (22 Jul 2022) and Leader's reply (2 Nov 2022)
summary: CASH's open letter, signed by Angela Fonso after its 'Air Pollution in Southall is a Health Emergency' webinar, says the site air monitors are 'not fit for purpose' (no VOC monitoring, badly sited), cites Brunel soil findings on lead/copper, and lists demands. The council reply lists actions taken since 2021 and rejects most of the demands, saying an abatement notice would 'certainly fail'.
notes: Reply dated 2 Nov 2022 sent on FOI-office letterhead. Webinar recording: youtu.be/HrblHG9Z_Q8.

title: Letter from Cllr Peter Mason (new Leader) to CASH setting out seven-point plan
summary: The day after he became Leader, Mason told CASH the council had too often seemed to be 'batting for the developers'. He instructed officers to commission legal advice on an abatement notice, involve CASH in independent air monitoring, work with Centric Lab, review Berkeley sponsorship and lobby government.
quote: Too often, it has seemed – rightly or wrongly – like the council is batting for the developers and not for residents.
notes: Part of the 'Southall Gasworks correspondence' archive https://www.ealing.gov.uk/downloads/download/6227/southall_gasworks_correspondence, which also lists letters to CASH of 7 Jun, 12 Jul, 2 Sep, 18 Oct 2021, 2 Aug and 24 Aug 2023, plus letters to Berkeley Group (21 Jun 2021), LB Hillingdon (21 Jun 2021) and Virendra Sharma MP (9 Jul 2021); those were not all captured. The CASH letters of 19 and 24 May 2021 that the 7 June reply mentions are not published there.

title: Southall Gasworks correspondence (Ealing Council download index)
summary: Index page of the Leader's published letters about the gasworks, 11 PDFs dated May 2021 to Aug 2023, most addressed to CASH.
notes: Uncaptured items worth fetching next: to_cash_7_june_2021 (id 16464), to_cash_12_july_2021 (16565), to_cash_2_september_2021 (16686), to_cash_18_october_2021 (16849), to_cash_2_august_2023 (19099), to_berkley_group_21_june_2021 (16465; says CASH was in talks with scientific organisations), to_virendra_sharma_mp_9_july_2021 (16564), to_cllr_ian_edwards_21_june_2021 (16462).

title: Letter from Cllr Peter Mason to CASH re Citizens Tribunal
summary: Short reply to Angela Fonso and CASH saying the council's Citizens Tribunal is independent and the Leader will not direct what it looks at. It follows a 2 Aug 2023 letter on Berkeley Group sponsorship of council events.
notes: Not saved as a separate file because it is short and is summarised here.

title: Cllr Peter Mason reply to Zack Polanski AM (Warren Farm; Southall Gasworks & CASH)
summary: Replying to an open letter from the Green AM, Mason restates the seven-point plan and says an abatement notice would lead to 'almost certain failure' in court. He says the council could not have shown a statutory nuisance even when odours were at their worst during soil-hospital operations.
quote: the Council would not have been able to demonstrate that a statutory nuisance had occurred, even when the foul smells from the remediation of soil at the Gasworks site were at their most acute
notes: Polanski's open letter itself not located.

title: Advice in respect of the Southall Waterside development and the F.M. Conway site (counsel's opinion, Stuart Jessop)
publisher: Ealing Council (counsel: Stuart Jessop, 6 Pump Court)
summary: Counsel's opinion to Ealing on its statutory-nuisance duties. It names CASH as alleging odour nuisance and records that CASH commissioned the Centric Lab report, which counsel criticises (sample of 10) while recommending a fresh PHE report that addresses it. It concludes the council was entitled to rely on PHE 2019 and to find no statutory nuisance.
notes: Instructions dated 6 Nov 2019, so commissioned under Julian Bell's leadership. Published later (by Nov 2022 per Mason letter). Counsel relied on instructions and expressly did not review the underlying material.

title: Updated counsel's opinion on Southall Waterside / FM Conway (Stuart Jessop), July 2021
summary: Second opinion commissioned under Mason's plan. It again finds no evidence of statutory nuisance or prejudice to health on the PHE 2019 and 2020 reports. It flags a mismatch between residents' strength of feeling and the very low complaint numbers (two in 2021) and suggests smell diaries. It notes that CASH or residents could bring their own s.82 EPA proceedings, and puts the cost of a contested abatement notice well above GBP 100k.
notes: Para 70: 'The contaminated land officer has had no correspondence from CASH and no evidence ... submitted'. Mentions the PHE report of July 2020.

title: Southall Broadway Ward Forum 29 July 2019 — Air quality in Southall, concerns about health and the odour
summary: Council briefing summarising PHE's interim health risk assessment (v3, 9 July 2019) of Atkins VOC data from Jan 2018 to May 2019. It says the soil hospital closed in March 2019, that there is 'unlikely to be a direct toxicological risk', and that the EA's odour recommendations had been met by the developer.
notes: Does not name CASH. Mentions a Cadent-controlled part of the site to be remediated off-site.

title: Air Pollution: Brownfield Redevelopment (Commons oral question, Defra)
summary: The Southall MP (speaker names not in the extraction; almost certainly Virendra Sharma) says constituents 'feel choked' by gasworks remediation fumes and asks why the EA and PHE are not empowered to act. The minister replies it is a matter for the local authority and the Mayor.
notes: CASH not named. Speaker identities unverified.

title: Funding studies into chemicals released by redevelopment (MQ 2023/1854, Zack Polanski)
summary: Polanski asks the Mayor to fund an extension of Imperial College's (Ian Mudway) Southall study to other gasworks. Sadiq Khan declines, saying he has no powers over contaminated land and that Ealing is responsible; he notes the 2010 mayoral overturn of Ealing's refusal.
notes: Question asked at MQT 18 May 2023. CASH not named.

title: Written evidence AIR0008 — AGHAST (Marie Sansford) to Environmental Audit Committee Air Pollution Inquiry
summary: Brighton gasworks campaign's submission cites Southall as a cautionary case. It says Berkeley Group acknowledged to AGHAST in August 2023 that siting the Southall soil hospital against garden walls was 'a mistake'. It also says Southall residents were told the smells came from their own detergents or smoking.
quote: Berkeley Group acknowledged to AGHAST in August 2023 that this was a mistake and said they are still learning how to best decontaminate ex-gasworks sites.
notes: Undated in extraction; references a 2025 planning appeal, so submitted 2025 or later. CASH not named. Claim about Berkeley's admission is AGHAST's account, not verified.

title: Boris Johnson's toxic legacy means residents think they're being gassed at front door
summary: National feature on residents' illnesses near Southall Waterside, framing the development as Johnson's 2010 mayoral call-in. It reports that CASH, founded by Angela Fonso, is preparing legal action with support from Jo Sidhu QC, and carries council and Berkeley responses.
quote: Local mum Angela Fonso, 51, founded CASH. “Depending on the direction of the wind, some days are worse than others,” she says.
notes: The article referenced in CrowdJustice Update 2. Photo caption spells her name 'Fonzo'.

title: 'We demand to be heard over Southall Waterside health concerns'
summary: Residents, including Angela Fonso of CASH, criticise Ealing for postponing a promised public meeting until after the EU elections because of purdah rules. The report details PHE findings that naphthalene was regularly above guideline values at the site boundary.
quote: Mrs Fonso is part of Clean Air for Southall and Hayes (CASH) and said residents wanted a public meeting with “people with decision making powers”.
notes: Links to earlier getwestlondon pieces: 'theres-terrible-smell-southall-residents-14906072', 'southall-mums-sneaky-protest-over-15030431' (17 Aug 2018), 'health-experts-called-investigate-hideous-15373478' — not fetched.

title: Residents prepare court challenge over redevelopment of London gasworks site
summary: Reports the campaign's planned public-nuisance action, fronted by Jo Sidhu QC, ahead of the 10 July 2019 public meeting. It quotes PHE that naphthalene 'should urgently be reduced' and notes Fonso's demand for independent monitoring and removal of a Berkeley manager as a school governor.
quote: “We will demand that there is independent air quality monitoring of the site and steps to reduce naphthalene levels,” said Angela Fonso, from the local campaign group.
notes: Says the Observer spoke to 50 residents.

title: Southall Gasworks Meeting: Where is Council Support for Residents?
summary: Account of the 10 July 2019 public meeting at the Dominion Centre (200+ residents) with council, Berkeley, EA and PHE, chaired by Peter Mason and opened by Julian Bell. It describes broken promises and an angry meeting that ended with no next steps, and notes CASH's crowdfunded legal plans.
quote: The community group Clean Air for Southall and Hayes (CASH) is now planning to take the developer and Ealing Council to court and have launched a crowd-funding campaign to help with legal costs.
notes: States a full-length 1h30 video of the meeting exists (link not captured). Ealing Today also reported this meeting ('Furious Meeting Over Southall Gasworks Redevelopment', 2019-07-12, ealingtoday.co.uk ...easouthallmeeting001.htm) but the live page and the 2019-09-20 Wayback capture returned no text.

title: Londoners claim toxic air from gasworks damaging their health
publisher: The Guardian (Jo Griffin, Maeve Shearlaw, Kyri Evangelou)
summary: Year-long Guardian investigation following CASH. Of 48 residents returning questionnaires, all reported breathing problems. Prof Roy Harrison said naphthalene data 'well exceeded' PHE guidelines, and the piece covers Centric Lab's susceptibility report.
quote: “I don’t believe this environmental injustice would happen in a more affluent white area.”
notes: Quote is Angela Fonso. Notes an air quality expert's Jan 2020 assessment that levels threatened health and AM Onkar Sahota's call for CASH seats on a monitoring appointment panel.

title: Is my neighbourhood poisoning me? Living in the shadow of a gasworks redevelopment (video, 14:45)
summary: Guardian documentary on Southall residents and the gasworks remediation, published with the 27 Aug 2020 article. The Guardian's 22 Sep 2020 piece says it prompted residents near the Hornsey and Bow sites to come forward.
notes: Not fetched directly; metadata from search result and embeds in Guardian articles. Not in the existing video list.

title: Residents demand new clean air rules for former gasworks sites in England
summary: Launch of Gasworks Communities United, an alliance of residents near the Southall, Hornsey, Lea Bridge and east Brighton gasworks sites demanding independent assessment of remediation. Angela Fonso is quoted as a GCU member and Southall coordinator, and Siân Berry comments.
quote: “Our experience in Southall shows there must be independent assessment of remediation strategies, better scrutiny by the local council and more accountability to residents,” said Angela Fonso

title: Scientists to examine health fears at west London luxury development
summary: Imperial College (Dr Ian Mudway) biomonitoring study, funded via the NIHR unit for chemical and radiation hazards, will deploy about 50 samplers and collect blood and urine from Southall residents. Fonso, described as CASH coordinator, welcomes it. Notes the APPG on gasworks redevelopment chaired by Virendra Sharma has disbanded.
quote: “This research project is a massive step forward for us. At last we might start to uncover why so many residents are facing these health issues.”
notes: Quote is Angela Fonso. Results of the Imperial study not located in this pass.

title: Families hit out at London gasworks redevelopment
summary: Early Observer report on parents' claims that weak pollution regulation at the Southall brownfield site endangers children. AGHAST's evidence cites it as reporting high naphthalene and an HSE demand for action.
notes: Not fetched; metadata from search snippet only. Whether CASH is named is unverified.

title: Air Pollution & Health in Southall, London (Centric Lab report, co-produced with CASH)
summary: Centric Lab's three-month pro-bono study with CASH argues that the guidelines PHE used did not account for the Southall community's susceptibility (chronic physical and psychosocial stressors). It calls for stricter guidelines and a cross-sectional health study.
quote: In the following co-produced report with Clean Air for Southall & Hayes, we put gathering evidence to highlight the susceptibility of the Southall community and the need for stricter air pollution guidelines.
notes: Page date 2025-02-17 is the web-page (re)publication; counsel's opinions say the report was produced in 2020 and commissioned by CASH. Full report sits behind a download form (not submitted, per read-only rule). The page calls the developer 'St. Williams Homes LLP'. Summary page added from CASH's copy of the report (user's Drive).

title: Community Health Impact Assessment: Centric Lab (CHIA scenario case study)
summary: Case study of the community health impact assessment (CHIA) template co-developed by Centric Lab and CASH from 2022. It says the template is now a toolkit and learning programme documented in peer-reviewed journals.
quote: “What if the HIA (Health Impact Assessment( was designed by people like us, would the approaches have been different; would we have fallen so ill?”
notes: Mason's Sept 2023 letter also refers to Centric Lab's Health Impact Assessment Toolkit.

title: Ealing: 'Stop the Poisoning' demonstration to demand evaluation of dangerous air pollution at Southall Gasworks
summary: Notice of a Gasworks Communities United protest at West Ham station on 26 Sep 2021. It lists GCU's three demands and says Ealing refused to serve an abatement notice despite hundreds of complaints.
quote: The group Clean Air for Southall and Hayes (CASH), comprising of Hayes and Southall residents, affected by the noxious odours from Southall Waterside, have been campaigning for better air quality monitoring in Ealing.

title: Southall locals stage protest over air pollution from two incinerators in a residential area
summary: CASH-organised protest at Balfour Industrial Estate, Johnson Street, over incinerator smoke, showing the group's later broadening beyond the gasworks. David Marsden recounts co-founding the group with Angela Fonso and the 2019 Dominion Centre meeting of '250 to 300 people'.
quote: “that’s when, together with Angela, my neighbour and a few other people who live locally, we decided to form a campaign group to get clean air for my son”
notes: Key source for CASH's founding story (Marsden + Fonso). A companion preview article of 21 Oct 2022 exists on ealing.news.

title: Southall Waterside Stinks! – Local working class resistance against soil and air pollution
summary: Left-wing workers' group blog describing early 2018 actions: leafleting, weekly protests, an autumn public meeting, disruption of Berkeley's AGM and of a Labour CLP meeting attended by the council leader. It directs readers to the CASH Facebook page and petition.
quote: Get in touch with the Clean Air for Southall and Hayes campaign
notes: Contains unsourced allegations about the then council leader and Berkeley hospitality; treat as advocacy.
